name: Classical Marxism
summary: Classical Marxism is the theory of Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels that history is driven by class struggle rooted in how society produces its goods, and that capitalism exploits wage labour and will be replaced through proletarian revolution. A transitional dictatorship of the proletariat would abolish private ownership of the means of production and lead to a stateless, classless communism distributing by need.
scope: Marx and Engels's own work from the Communist Manifesto (1848) to the Critique of the Gotha Programme (1875) and The Civil War in France (1871). It excludes Leninism, Stalinism, Maoism, Western Marxism and later theories of imperialism, dependency and cultural hegemony; statements on those topics are mostly inferred at low confidence.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Never addressed by Marx; inferred from the Manifesto's free public education and state provision of common needs under a workers' state.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: No minimum wage in the texts; an adherent would back wage gains as part of class organisation while holding that only abolishing wage labour solves the problem.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The Manifesto describes market production as producing recurrent crises of overproduction, and the Commune text calls for production regulated on a common plan.

public-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto's transitional measures put credit, transport and communications in state hands and expand state-owned factories.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The Manifesto's second measure is a heavy progressive or graduated income tax.

unions-good.rationale: The Commune text endorses workers' associations, and Marx treated union organisation as part of class formation, though not a route to abolishing wage labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: The theory is summed up as abolition of private property; bourgeois property is the target of the revolution.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Reforms like factory legislation were welcomed as gains, but regulation was never the aim; inferred as mild agreement.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; the dependency argument is a bourgeois view of poverty, which the Manifesto traces to capitalist relations, so an adherent leans against cuts.

worker-ownership.rationale: The Commune would hand closed workshops to workers' associations, though the classical goal is common ownership by society rather than firm-by-firm ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from hostility to the bourgeois state's repressive apparatus, mild since a workers' state also coerces its opponents.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed and no principle bears on it; adherents have no stated position.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Marx treated prostitution as a product of bourgeois family and capital but never addressed its legal status; inferred split.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would be split between opposing bourgeois censorship and suppressing reaction.

strong-leader.rationale: The Commune model stresses accountable, recallable delegates rather than a leader bypassing deliberation; inferred.

state-harmful.rationale: Marx held the state a class instrument that must be used by the proletariat in transition and later withers, so it is neither simply harmful nor necessary forever.

limit-guns.rationale: The Commune replaced the army with the armed people, so an adherent leans against strict limits on workers' arms; inferred.

empower-police-military.rationale: The Commune's first act abolished the standing army in favour of the armed people and treated the state machine as a parasite.

decide-locally.rationale: The Manifesto centralises means of production in the state, though the Commune model is communal; inferred as a mild disagreement.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the view that crime and character spring from social circumstances.

traditional-family.rationale: The Manifesto argues the bourgeois family rests on capital and private gain and will vanish with capital.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred as support for legal equality from the view of marriage as a historical, class-shaped institution.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the critique of the bourgeois family and women as instruments of production.

more-religion-public.rationale: Marx wanted to liberate the conscience from the witchery of religion and the Commune disestablished churches.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a core theme; inferred as support from the emancipatory goal, though class is the primary axis.

gender-social-construct.rationale: The Manifesto treats the family and women's position as historically produced by property relations; inferred.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The Manifesto says national one-sidedness and narrow-mindedness become impossible as the world market develops.

gradual-change.rationale: The classical view is that social orders end through revolutionary rupture when production relations fetter productive forces.

reduce-immigration.rationale: The proletariat is held to have no country and national antagonisms are to fade; inferred.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Anachronistic; Marx was internationalist but saw existing states as class instruments, so no clear answer.

free-trade.rationale: The Manifesto calls free trade the single remaining freedom of the bourgeoisie, serving capital rather than everyone.

nation-first.rationale: The Manifesto states that working men have no country and that national antagonisms will vanish.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from viewing bourgeois states' foreign actions as serving capital.

open-borders.rationale: The proletariat's internationalism and the fading of national antagonisms point toward open borders in the end state.

limit-growth.rationale: Communism is premised on developing productive forces to abundance; ecological limits were not a theme here.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from conscious social planning of production.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Technology develops productive forces but under capitalism deskills and impoverishes; benefit depends on property relations.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Anachronistic with no principle bearing on it.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolution by the proletariat is the classical route from capitalism, with the bourgeoisie producing its own grave-diggers.

experts-over-public.rationale: The theory rests on class consciousness and self-emancipation of workers; inferred against rule by experts.

central-planning.rationale: Both the Manifesto and the Commune text call for production under a common plan instead of market anarchy.

socialized-markets.rationale: Marx envisaged ending wage labour and commodity exchange, so markets even among workers' firms are not the aim.

land-value-tax.rationale: Land rents go to public purposes in the Manifesto, but a single tax replacing others reformist; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of all right of inheritance.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; the Manifesto makes labour equally obligatory and the lower phase pays by labour contributed, so unconditional income sits poorly.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: The sources treat free trade as a bourgeois freedom but give no verdict on tariffs; inferred split.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in a national bank and expands state factories under a common plan.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Commune text aims to turn land and capital into instruments of associated labour, not to spread small property.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wage labour is to end, and the higher phase distributes by need; abolition of money follows by implication.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: The Manifesto demands centralising credit in a state bank with monopoly.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The Manifesto holds classes are antagonists; bodies uniting employers and workers contradict that.

one-party-rule.rationale: Classical Marxism posits a class dictatorship with accountable delegates, not one party ruling the state, a later Leninist idea.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Marx demands a democratic republic and attacks hereditary privilege.

democracy-best.rationale: Marx held the democratic republic to be the political form for proletarian rule, but treated bourgeois democracy as class-limited.

direct-votes.rationale: Marx called direct legislation a mere echo of bourgeois democratic demands, yet the Commune bound delegates to constituents.

workers-councils.rationale: The Commune is Marx's model political form rather than a parliament; later council theory extends it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Class interest outranks national claims in the sources; inferred as contingent.

natural-rulers.rationale: The Commune made officials accountable, revocable and paid workmen's wages, abolishing hereditary or natural privilege.

political-violence-never.rationale: The Manifesto envisages revolution and despotic inroads on property rights.

war-builds-character.rationale: The Commune text blames war's originators and rejects the peasants' blood tax; inferred opposition to glorifying war.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Commune decreed disestablishment and disendowment of churches, and Marx excluded church from schools.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The Manifesto calls religion and law bourgeois prejudices and Marx wanted conscience freed from religion.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Not addressed; privatising coercion contradicts the view of the state as class instrument to be taken over by workers.

military-superiority.rationale: The Commune abolished the standing army and was internationalist; the sources reject militarism.

ethnic-nation.rationale: National antagonisms fade and the proletariat has no country, so ethnic purity has no place.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The Manifesto opens by declaring all hitherto existing history a history of class struggles.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Marx called equal right bourgeois right and unequal for unequal people; the end goal is distribution by need, not equal shares.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between communal property sympathy and class priority.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Marx criticised colonial plunder but did not address reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Class, not civilisation, is the primary unit; the Manifesto expects national barriers to dissolve.

self-interest-moral.rationale: The Manifesto condemns the bourgeoisie for reducing relations to naked self-interest and cash payment.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Marx treated rights as bourgeois but sought free development of each; no clear side.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Marx's treatment of nature centres on human production; inferred indifferent.

limit-population.rationale: Poverty is attributed to capitalist relations rather than numbers; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The Manifesto credits the bourgeoisie with creating vast productive forces that communism will inherit.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Productive development is a precondition for communism; inferred, though disruption is blamed on capital.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic; no basis in the sources.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from accountable, recallable human delegates.

restore-past-order.rationale: The Manifesto praises the bourgeoisie for sweeping away feudal ties and treats a return as reactionary.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Marx held ideas arise from class position and material conditions; inferred against dismissing ideology.

direct-action.rationale: The classical view is for class political action culminating in revolution including organised politics; inferred.

means-match-ends.rationale: Marx accepted a revolutionary dictatorship and despotic measures as means towards a stateless society.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Primitive communism is a superseded stage; communism builds on capitalist productive forces.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Marx's higher phase requires ending the enslaving subordination to the division of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Gotha critique states the higher phase principle: from each according to ability, to each according to needs.

production-for-use.rationale: Communism ends production for profit and exchange so labour becomes life's prime want; stated in outline.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Surplus value from unpaid labour is the source of profit in Marx's account of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Marx names the revolutionary dictatorship of the proletariat as the state form of the transition.

collective-farming.rationale: The Manifesto cultivates land under a common plan and combines agriculture with industry.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marx tied crises to conquest of new markets, but the full imperialism thesis is Leninist.

taxation-theft.rationale: The Manifesto demands heavy progressive taxation as a transitional measure.

harm-principle.rationale: The Manifesto accepts despotic inroads on property rights; inferred rejection of a liberal limit.

individual-rights-only.rationale: SEP reports Marx saw liberal rights as protecting separate individuals and not true freedom; real freedom lies in community.

conscription.rationale: The Manifesto proposes industrial armies and the Commune an armed citizenry; inferred mild agreement.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Marx sought real freedom through democratic communal life, not exit rights.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers is the market logic Marx opposed.

positive-liberty.rationale: Marx held real freedom needs material emancipation and human community, not just non-interference.

media-academia-power.rationale: Ideology serves the ruling class which holds economic power; media and academia are superstructure, not the power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not addressed directly; character is explained by circumstance and social relations.

organic-representation.rationale: The Commune model is revocable delegates elected by the people, not corporate bodies.

total-state.rationale: Marx demanded government and church be excluded from schools and wanted the state subordinate to society.

national-rebirth.rationale: Marx views national narrowness as fading; inferred against nationalist rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Nations are to dissolve in class internationalism; the Commune opposed war.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: The Manifesto praises the bourgeoisie for ending feudal personal ties.

bound-labor.rationale: Feudal bonds of labour are seen as swept away; the proletariat is to abolish all class exploitation.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Ideology is the dominant class's ideas shaped by control of mental production.

universal-morality.rationale: The Manifesto calls law, morality and religion bourgeois prejudices; scholarship says Marx rejected trans-epochal morals.

single-common-good.rationale: Society is divided by antagonistic class interests so there is no single common good.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred against nation-state projects from proletarian internationalism.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from de-emphasis of nationality.

workplace-democracy.rationale: The Commune text calls for associated workers to run production.

school-vouchers.rationale: Marx wanted schooling free of church and state influence; marketised vouchers are inferred as opposed.

economic-freedom.rationale: Marx held political emancipation is not human emancipation without transforming economic life, the reverse of this claim.

rule-by-example.rationale: Marx wants accountable institutions and not rulers' virtue; inferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: Class priority qualifies national claims; split.

force-without-un.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred opposition to bourgeois-state military adventure.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Marx wanted to liberate conscience from religion, though not reason as the sole guide.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The proletariat has no country so benefits by nationality contradict internationalism.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The Manifesto makes labour equally obligatory for all, which suggests agreement.

class-collaboration.rationale: The Manifesto presents classes as antagonists in a struggle, not partners.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred that culture is a product of class society and not to be destroyed.

dominated-front.rationale: Marx's frame is class, not national blocs.

workers-nation.rationale: The Manifesto says working men have no country, though proletariat must first organise nationally.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The Manifesto sees the bourgeois family as built on women's subordination; inferred.

ban-interest.rationale: Marx centralises credit in a state bank rather than banning interest; inferred.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not addressed; incompatible with class solidarity.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The Manifesto defines political power as the organised power of one class for oppressing another.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Marx and Engels wrote before this debate; nothing in their principles favours or opposes particular fuels, so the answer is neutral and inferred.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: The proletariat is internationalist and the sources do not expect conformity to a national culture.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory outside the class analysis.

national-mission.rationale: National missions contradict the classless internationalism of the Manifesto.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The Manifesto treats the wife as an instrument of production in the bourgeois family; inferred.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The state is described as the bourgeoisie's committee; corruption itself is not the theme.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not addressed; opposed to emancipatory aims.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The Commune made officials accountable; inferred.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The Manifesto's measures expand state economic direction massively.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Not stated as moral doctrine, but class abolition implies equality; inferred.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The Manifesto envisages revolution among advanced countries and abolishing nations; inferred.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Marx and Engels did not set out a doctrine on settler states, and adherents split between condemning colonial plunder and treating class as primary.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Inferred from separating church from state.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Marx opposed religious coercion but also religion; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religious taboo with no basis in materialism.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Marx insisted government and church be excluded from influence on schools.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The state withers as classes disappear; the encirclement doctrine is later.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Commune's elected recallable officials imply consent; inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist aims are not Marx's; inferred.

population-transfer.rationale: Inferred against national exclusion from internationalism.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The Manifesto endorses revolutionary force and despotic inroads.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Class struggle drives history, not competition between peoples.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Communists were themselves targets of bans; inferred.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Wage dependence is domination in Marx's account; inferred.

separated-powers.rationale: The Commune combined executive and legislative functions in an accountable body; inferred.

vanguard-party.rationale: Marx favoured organising revolutionaries but the Leninist vanguard doctrine is later; contested.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Proletarian interests are the priority, though framed as class not charity.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Public housing policy is absent from the classical texts; a split between opposing property sales and valuing workers' homeownership leaves this neutral.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The Manifesto traces workers' immiseration to capitalist industry, not population.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Inferred from national antagonisms being seen as class-driven.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: The Commune used election and recall, not lottery.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The proletarian dictatorship is extra-legal against the old ruling classes; inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not stated; Commune emphasised accountable governance, so inferred disagreement.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Commune used the armed people, not party command.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Inferred from lack of a country for workers.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The Commune made public service work at workman's wage.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Marx sought disciplined organisation; the concept is later Leninist.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Anachronistic; internationalist but no stated position on bourgeois supranational unions.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The Commune replaced the standing army and executive with accountable delegates.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Marx opposed church privilege and property.

clerical-rule.rationale: Opposes religious authority on conscience and schooling.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The Commune held war's originators responsible; the slogan itself is Leninist.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not stated; opposed to church control of morals.

recall-officials.rationale: The Commune's officials were responsible and revocable at short terms.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Marx aimed at common ownership of land, not each family holding property; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Commune's first decree replaced the standing army with the armed people.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Manifesto aims to reduce the town and country divide, not idealise rural life.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The texts give no rule on borders imposed by outside powers; class priority over national claims leaves the answer neutral and inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: The Manifesto treats the bourgeois world market as pulling barbarian nations into civilisation, a stage view.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from reformist-humanist stance.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from free public education and critique of bourgeois family.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Marx excluded church influence from schools and was a materialist.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Marx and Engels did not address sexual media regulation, and no core principle settles it, so the answer is neutral and inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Inferred from rejection of nationality as basis.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Marx treated religion as illusion; inferred against special exemptions.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: The Manifesto's end state is the free development of each; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Inferred from internationalist critique of finance and war debts.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Political emancipation is not human emancipation without economic transformation.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The dictatorship is a transition over classes, not a developmental device; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The classical texts speak of class solidarity and not of aid between states, which they treat as instruments of ruling classes; inferred neutral.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Marx wanted accountable, revocable officials and a democratic republic but never discussed how a single head of state is chosen; neutral.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The Manifesto puts credit under state control with a monopoly national bank.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Inferred from rejection of territorial nationalism.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes bourgeois property rather than conditioning it; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Anachronistic; Marx died before the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Environmental risk regulation is anachronistic for 19th-century Marxism and no principle clearly decides it; neutral inferred answer.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Inferred from Commune's support for exiles and oppressed.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The Commune disestablished and disendowed churches.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Marx rejected hereditary or symbolic rulers in favour of accountable officials.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Marx and Engels subordinated national questions to the interests of the proletariat case by case, so no general answer on using force against secession is documented.

region-keeps-system.rationale: This one-country-two-systems idea is anachronistic and the classical texts give no basis for judging it; neutral and inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Marx opposed religion and hereditary privilege.

flat-income-tax.rationale: The Manifesto demands a heavy progressive income tax.

character-from-environment.rationale: Marx held human nature has constant and historically variable elements shaped by material conditions.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The Commune made officials answerable and revocable.

space-expansion.rationale: Space exploration lies wholly outside the classical texts, which only value developing productive forces generally; neutral and inferred.

leader-cult.rationale: Inferred from accountable officials paid workmen's wages.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody rules are unaddressed; the Manifesto's critique of the bourgeois family does not settle how courts should divide parenting time.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Marx saw the dictatorship as lasting until classes disappear, but later claims are Maoist; unsettled.

land-redistribution.rationale: The Manifesto expropriates landed property for public purposes, but gives it to the state, not to farmers.

refugee-return.rationale: The classical texts do not address refugee return rights; internationalism and solidarity with exiles suggest sympathy but the issue is too far for a position.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: National antagonisms are to disappear; ethnic claims contradict this.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Marx wanted conscience free from religion.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from opposition to religion in law.

common-currency.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit nationally but nothing addresses shared currencies among states; adherents would be split and the answer is neutral.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Historical materialism holds production relations shape society and consciousness.

ban-cartels.rationale: Marx saw concentration as a development to be inherited by socialism, not reversed.

no-bailouts.rationale: Marx saw the state as managing the bourgeoisie's common affairs, so bailouts are expected, but he gave no verdict on whether they should happen; neutral.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Marx criticised bourgeois courts and law as class expressions but also doubted majority rule inside bourgeois states, so there is no clear answer.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The world market is treated as progressive.

moral-incentives.rationale: Higher phase makes labour life's prime want, though the lower phase pays by labour.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolution requires fettered productive forces and class consciousness, not a small armed group.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: The Manifesto lists abolition of inheritance and denounces feudal privilege.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: The Manifesto notes bourgeois pressure on barbarian nations, but justifying rule is not its position; inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: The proletariat has no country; national pride is bourgeois.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Affirmative action is a modern policy debate absent from the classical texts; class-focused adherents might oppose it but others would support it, so neutral.

public-money-creation.rationale: The Manifesto centralises credit in the national bank.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The Manifesto describes crises as growing and the bourgeoisie as producing its own grave-diggers.

delink-world-market.rationale: The world market is seen as progressive, so delinking is a later view.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Marx treats liberal rights as limited; inferred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Marx condemned colonial plunder but never discussed the legal status of colonial treaties, so the answer is neutral and inferred.

minority-veto.rationale: Commune decisions bind via majority; inferred.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Marx wanted Commune as working body, not a parliamentary one; unclear.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Animal ethics is not a theme of the classical texts, which centre on human production and society; neutral and inferred.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use for food and research is not addressed in the classical texts, so there is no documented position and the answer is neutral.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalist charity is a form of class rule in Manifesto.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Class struggle is political and workers must act.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Ideology and religion are said to stabilise class societies; applied to mass media by inference.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Ideology stabilises class societies, though the consent theory is Gramscian.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: The Manifesto notes the world market remakes nations in bourgeois image; extraction theory is later.

native-born-offices.rationale: The Commune admitted foreigners as full participants.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from rejection of national claims.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: The classical texts do not discuss political leadership by indigenous descendants; communal property sympathy and class priority pull opposite ways.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed in sources; inferred from class analysis.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument debates are modern and absent from the classical texts; adherents could favour preserving history or removing symbols of rule, so neutral.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Gender-specific programmes for boys and men are a modern debate; classical Marxism offers no stated position and the answer is neutral.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The classical texts do not address domestic violence statistics or services; neutral and inferred from the absence of any principle.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The Commune abolished the standing army.

filial-duty.rationale: Marx and Engels criticised the bourgeois family but did not discuss duties of adult children, so no firm answer exists and this is neutral.

office-by-exam.rationale: The Commune used election and recall.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from critique of bourgeois family.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Commune officials were responsible and revocable at short terms.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from collective provision and anti-market orientation.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The Manifesto abolishes property in land with rents to the public.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The classical texts do not address parliamentary budget control; the Commune's accountable assembly suggests sympathy but Marx also mocked parliaments, so neutral.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The disparate impact standard is a modern legal doctrine unaddressed in the classical texts; neutral and inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Commodity fetishism and alienation criticise commodity-driven life.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Marx and Engels supported some insurgent movements abroad but also opposed bourgeois states' interventions; no general rule is documented, so neutral.

corporate-influence.rationale: The Manifesto says the state is a committee managing the bourgeoisie's affairs.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The classical texts do not address foreign funding of NGOs, media or universities, and sovereignty is not a Marxist concern; neutral and inferred.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Population policy through family incentives is not discussed in the classical texts, and the Marxist critique of the family does not settle it; neutral.

residents-only-property.rationale: Marx wanted common ownership of land and no national barriers, but did not address local purchasing limits; neutral and inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Inferred from obligation of all to labour.

democratic-peace.rationale: Marx held bourgeois states' wars arise from capital; inferred.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Marx said right is no higher than the economic structure; inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Industrial versus craft unionism arose after Marx; his general support for workers' combination does not settle the form, so the answer is neutral.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Marx expected family forms to change but did not decide on legal marriage.

local-production.rationale: The world market is seen as progressive.

informal-organisation.rationale: Marx attempted organised bodies like the International.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The tribute system is a premodern East Asian practice absent from Marxism, which treats national hierarchies as class questions; lightly inferred disagreement.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The Manifesto states communists do not abolish personal property earned by labour.

defeat-communism.rationale: Communists seek to establish communism worldwide; coexistence is not the question for them.

religion-illusion.rationale: Marx called religion the opium of the people and wanted conscience liberated from it; SEP describes it as a response to material alienation that will fade.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The Manifesto credits the bourgeoisie with creating vast productive forces and the proletariat that will succeed it.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Marx and Engels tie the subordination of women to private property and the bourgeois family, so emancipation requires abolishing those conditions.

socialized-care.rationale: The Manifesto demands public education for all children and ends the bourgeois family, implying socialised provision of care.

purge-loanwords.rationale: The Manifesto says national one-sidedness becomes impossible and a world literature arises, so national linguistic purism is rejected.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred: Marx treated state agreements as instruments of class power, not lasting binding promises.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: Marx rejected small utopian communities as a path, though the Commune model federated self-governing communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's opposition to national exploitation and oppression of one nation by another.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Classical Marxism holds that communism is the successor to capitalism and the sound basis for society.

historical-land-claim.rationale: The Manifesto says workers have no country and sets class above national claims.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Marx and Engels's commitment to historical materialism and scientific analysis.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the tradition's hostility to bourgeois moral codes and state policing of private life, though Marx and Engels held no formal position.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The dictatorship of the proletariat suppresses counter-revolution, while the Commune model allows open politics, so adherents read it both ways.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Marx demanded freedom of conscience and the separation of church from state, and held that religion belongs to private life.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The Manifesto describes the bourgeoisie's world market and colonial expansion as exploitation of the weaker nations by the ruling class.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Marx treated religion as an expression of social conditions, so an Islamic duty is not part of his theory, though he backed anti-colonial resistance.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Marx held religion to be ideology and rejected religious law as a source of legitimacy.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Paris Commune model has officials on workmen's wages, elected and recallable by the people, with producers running affairs themselves.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Marx and Engels saw class as the primary driver and other oppressions as flowing from it, so they would not treat the three as equal.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the tradition's commitment to human emancipation and equal rights.

assisted-dying.rationale: Anachronistic and never addressed; inferred from Marx's rejection of religious morality and his emphasis on individual freedom.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Manifesto says the proletarian revolution is a class struggle that divides society, not one that blends left and right ideas.

alienated-labor.rationale: Alienation of labour under capitalism is central to Marx's early work and is documented in the scholarship.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Anachronistic; Marx held that national and cultural antagonisms fade with class rule and that religion is a prejudice.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Marx treated religion as a product of society and the Manifesto calls it a bourgeois prejudice.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred from Marx's call for church and school to be separate from the state.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the tradition's pro-labour and anti-employer stance.

social-market-economy.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolishing bourgeois property and Marx saw the market as the root of exploitation, not something to be tempered.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Marx and Engels wanted standing armies replaced by an armed people, not an end to arms during the transition.

rich-first.rationale: The Manifesto aims to abolish private ownership rather than let some grow rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred from proletarian internationalism and hostility to bourgeois great-power rivalry; Marx did not address blocs as such.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Marx and Engels demanded abolition of inheritance and a democratic republic, rejecting hereditary rule.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising credit in the hands of the state by a national bank, not user-owned interest-free credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred: Marx and Engels opposed capitalist finance but wrote nothing on sovereign debt conditionality and held that reform within capitalism is limited.

property-franchise.rationale: The Manifesto aims to win the battle of democracy for the working class, which means universal suffrage, not property limits.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Inferred from Engels's linking of women's subordination to private property and his writing on humanity's relation to nature; the link is not Marx's own formulation.

reification.rationale: Marx's critique of commodity fetishism and alienation says social relations appear as relations between things that rule human beings.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Marx held that the ruling ideas are those of the ruling class, and the Manifesto treats bourgeois freedom as freedom of trade and property.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred: Marx treated bourgeois legality as class instrument and endorsed revolutionary dictatorship, while also demanding a democratic republic.

racial-franchise.rationale: The Manifesto holds that workers have no country and unites proletarians of all nations; racial limits on citizenship are alien to it.

online-participation.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Marx's demand for broad popular participation and the Commune's recallable officials.

open-government-data.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Commune's accountable, recallable officials answerable to the people.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Marx demanded that everyone be free to attend to religious needs without police interference and wanted church separated from the state.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Marx held that class, not religion, divides people; singling out a religious minority divides the proletariat.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Inferred: the Commune used elected, recallable delegates, but Marx did not discuss sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred: Marx saw religion as an illusion to be dissolved by changing material conditions, not reformed doctrinally.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Manifesto describes bourgeois property as the concentration of social power in few hands that dominates the many.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Marx and Engels never addressed it; inferred from their opposition to militarised class rule and stress on emancipation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Marx wanted religion to fade with material emancipation but, in the Gotha critique, demanded freedom of conscience from the state, not state-imposed atheism.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: The Commune made police accountable and the state is to wither away eventually, but the transitional workers' state still uses coercion; abolition at once is not their position.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the class-based politics of the Manifesto; communal power-sharing was not addressed.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's view that poverty is produced by class relations that must be abolished, not relieved by charity.

term-limits.rationale: Not addressed; the Commune's recall of officials suggests accountability but not term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: The Civil War in France praises the Commune's officials as revocable delegates subject to recall at any time.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Anachronistic; Marx and Engels did not address extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's call for equality and the abolition of class and gender subordination; religious offices not addressed.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's critique of the bourgeois family and subordination of women; marriage authority not discussed directly.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Marx held that workers have no country and the Manifesto calls for internationalism, so excluding resident workers from civic participation would be foreign to it; no local franchise question was addressed.

rent-control.rationale: The Manifesto's transitional measures include rent of land applied to public purposes, but Marx and Engels saw rent caps as palliatives that leave the housing question unsolved.

abolish-ip.rationale: Marx and Engels did not address patents; abolishing property in the means of production is central, but abolishing intellectual property as such is an inference.

uniformed-youth.rationale: The Commune model replaces the standing army with the armed people, and the Marxist outlook rejects state-drilled national-service youth organisations.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the opposition to militarism and the standing army, which the Commune replaced with a people's militia.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Manifesto's view that workers' internationalism opposes foreign military power over other peoples.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; Marx and Engels judged events by class and rarely by legal recognition, though their sympathy for oppressed peoples cuts toward agreement.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Marx's Gotha critique states that in the lower phase each receives according to labour contributed, and the Manifesto abolishes unearned property income.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Marx endorsed revolutionary violence and armed defence of the Commune, so he did not hold killing in defence absolutely wrong; the question is not addressed directly.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: The Manifesto (s1) treats nations as products of bourgeois development whose differences are vanishing, which rules out an ancient unbroken national identity; it does not discuss continuity directly.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Marx and Engels treated sex differences as largely natural and the division of labour by sex as rooted in biology; the constructionist claim is much later.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; the classical tradition treated women as a category within class, which later feminists criticised.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The Manifesto calls nationality a bourgeois product and religious sanctification a bourgeois ideology; honouring martyrs and saints of the nation is rejected.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Historical materialism (s6) explains politics through material class interests and treats religion as ideology, which rejects politics as a spiritual battle; the claim is not discussed directly.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: The Manifesto treats nationality as transient and does not envisage a national homeland as a diaspora's centre.

culture-before-state.rationale: For Marx the economic and class transformation comes first and culture follows from the material base.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; Marx criticised religion as ideology but a materialist would hardly insist on male God-language, so mild agreement is inferred.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Marx saw religion as a reflection of material conditions and did not judge it by feminist standards, though Engels praised the equality of early Christian communities.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Marx and Engels' internationalism (s1) and their aim of common ownership reject allocating economic life by nationality; majority-versus-minority ownership is not discussed.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Marx and Engels supported self-determination for some peoples (Poland, Ireland) but disliked small-nation separatism and favoured large units, so ethnic merging is not a Marxist aim.

independent-unions.rationale: Not a topic Marx and Engels developed as such; inferred from the Gotha critique's insistence that workers' organisations not be placed under state tutelage.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: The Manifesto states the first step of the revolution is to raise the proletariat to the position of ruling class.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from the Manifesto's free public education and the Commune's public provision of common services.

second-chamber.rationale: The Commune is described as a single working body, executive and legislative at once, with no second chamber.

municipal-property.rationale: The Manifesto and the Civil War in France call for common ownership by associated producers on a national plan, not for ownership by each locality.

confederal-coordination.rationale: The Civil War in France describes the Commune's national organisation as delegates with limited, revocable mandates sent from the communes.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred: Marx aimed at abolishing wage labour, and the Manifesto attacks the bourgeois family; neither endorses a family-wage settlement.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Never addressed and no principle clearly bears on it; adherents would be indifferent.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's enthusiasm for science and technology mastering nature once it serves the producers.

anonymous-payments.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising credit in the hands of the state in the transition, and communism abolishes money, leaving no place for untraceable private payment.

online-anonymity.rationale: Anachronistic; no principle in the sources clearly decides it.

person-over-state.rationale: The Manifesto's aim is an association in which the free development of each is the condition of the free development of all.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Marx's materialism treats religion and spiritual claims as products of material conditions, and the Manifesto treats religion as ideology.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred: the Civil War in France insists on national unity organised through the commune system rather than a sovereign federation of regions.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Manifesto's view that mastering nature through science raises productive forces.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto calls for gradually abolishing the distinction between town and country by spreading population more evenly.

racial-group-interests.rationale: The Manifesto holds that class, not race or nation, defines the proletariat's interests and that workers have no country.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from class internationalism: group pride of this kind is not part of the doctrine.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Inferred: the Civil War in France has the Commune abolish the standing army in favour of an armed people, but Marx also backed revolutionary and national-liberation wars.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Marx and Engels held that workers have no country and put class above nation, so they did not treat language and history as the basis of a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred from Marx's view of religion as an illusion and his rejection of confessional politics.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Marx and Engels treated nationalism as bourgeois and stressed class struggle rather than foreign plots.

free-public-college.rationale: The Manifesto demands free education for all children in public schools; extending this to higher education is an inference.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred from Marx's preference for planned social control of production over price tools within capitalism.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from Marx's remarks that society should hand the earth on improved to later generations.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Marx and Engels grounded politics in class, not in distinct gendered values.

arms-reduction.rationale: The Paris Commune replaced the standing army with the armed people, which implies hostility to large permanent armaments.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from the Commune's principle of public accountability, in contrast with secret state diplomacy.

capital-controls.rationale: The Manifesto calls for centralising credit in the hands of the state, which implies state control over finance.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Marx held the Commune should replace the standing army with the armed people, and the Manifesto's proletariat arms itself; a permanent state monopoly on arms was not the goal.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's claim that workers have no country and that wars among nations serve the bourgeoisie; Marx never set out a doctrine of soldier refusal.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Marx backed trade unions as schools of class organisation, though he thought wage bargaining alone could not end wage slavery; inferred from the Manifesto's account of workers combining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Never addressed; Marx saw wage supplements within capitalism as palliatives that leave exploitation intact, inferred from the Gotha critique of reformist demands.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the Manifesto's call for centralised credit in state hands, which implies no binding limit on a workers' state's borrowing.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Marx did not frame the issue as reforming international rules for developing countries; he sought world revolution to end capitalism, so a reform framing fits poorly.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Marx wrote after the Commune that the working class cannot simply lay hold of the ready-made state machinery but must break it and replace it with the Commune's form.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Marx and Engels claimed a scientific account of the transition to communism and criticised utopian blueprints, but they also refused to write recipes, and they expected a common planned economy rather than rival systems.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Marx criticised valuing nature through capital and exchange value, and held that capitalism's treatment of land and resources as commodities alienates and degrades them.

sacred-nation.rationale: The Manifesto (s1) says the workers have no country and treats national antagonisms as passing, which leaves no place for a sacred nation; sacredness is not discussed.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from the Manifesto's free public education for all children and the Gotha critique's view that education should be public.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not a classical Marxist concept; Marx wrote on colonial exploitation and on town against country, but the internal-colonialism thesis came later, so this is left neutral.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Marx rejected a fixed human essence, holding human nature to be the ensemble of social relations that changes with history, and he mocked natural-rights talk as bourgeois.

public-service-media.rationale: Never addressed; Marx defended a free press against censorship and the Manifesto calls for public control of communications, but he did not discuss public broadcasting.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Marx treated religion as an illusory consolation of alienated people that will fade, not as a vehicle of shared truth, so he would reject the claim that religions express one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not addressed; the Manifesto's measures call for state ownership of land rather than price supports for small proprietors, so this is inferred as a mild no.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Anachronistic; Marx backed an armed people and proletarian internationalism but never addressed deterrence, so there is no clear inference.

workers-own-party.rationale: The Manifesto says communists form the proletariat into a class and so into a political party, and Marx treats independent class politics as essential.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Manifesto's call to end women's status as mere instruments of production and from its hostility to oppressive custom.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed directly; the Manifesto proposes abolishing inheritance and private land ownership altogether, which cuts against the premise of equal inheritance, though equality of women is implied.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Never addressed; the Manifesto's treatment of nationality does not bear on how regional language varieties are named.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Anachronistic; Marx held that capitalist property relations cause such harms and that a planned common economy, not private lawsuits, would address them.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: The Manifesto attacks feudal and patriarchal relations, and the Commune model rests on elected, recallable officials, leaving no place for hereditary customary authority.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Marx's critique of capitalism's exhaustion of the soil and its subordination of social needs to private profit.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Marx saw crime and punishment as products of social conditions and criticised punitive state power, so fixed sentences are inferred as disfavoured.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Anachronistic; the Manifesto holds that workers have no country and stresses internationalism, so compulsion over a national language is inferred as unwelcome.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's stress on workers combining in unions as a class organisation, so compulsory solidarity fits better than voluntary dues.

voter-id.rationale: Inferred from the Commune's wider franchise and critique of bourgeois electoral machinery; the sources do not discuss voter ID.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the Gotha Critique's view that religion is a private matter and the state should not favour a creed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Marx held that bourgeois elections do not create popular rule and praised the Commune's recallable delegates as real democracy.

premarital-sex.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's attack on bourgeois marriage and the family as property relations.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Commune's press freedom and distrust of an unaccountable state.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from Marx's criticism in the Gotha Critique of welfare-style distribution as no answer to wage labour.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred; Marx and Engels backed women's emancipation, though the sources centre on class rather than suffrage.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Engels traced women's subordination to private property and class society, not to religion as the main cause.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the materialist view that social categories arise from social relations; the era's science differed.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from Marx's view that the state is a class instrument that should wither away, not a lead promoter of reforms.

homestead-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto calls for the abolition of bourgeois private property, and Marx treats original appropriation as conquest and force.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Marx's view that courts and the state serve the ruling class, though he backed Commune accountability.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The Manifesto treats religion as bourgeois ideology and says communism abolishes eternal truths and all religion.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's call for equal liability of all to labour and the abolition of the bourgeois family.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from Marx's defence of the Commune and workers' state against restoration, though he never saw a bureaucratic one.

indirect-election.rationale: The Civil War in France describes the Commune's plan of national bodies made up of delegates from local communal councils.

national-church-status.rationale: The Commune disestablished the church, and Marx praises this as part of dismantling the state's instruments of oppression.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Marx and Engels backed some national movements, such as Poland and Ireland, but subordinated nationality to class, and Engels disparaged others.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Marx and Engels treated national questions by their effect on the class struggle, not by a principle of local vote.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Anachronistic; the Manifesto says workers have no country and the classics never ruled on colonial borders.

simple-living.rationale: Inferred from Marx's view that communism rests on abundance, which rejects voluntary austerity as an ideal.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the Manifesto's internationalism, which opposes barriers by nationality or origin.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the Commune's replacement of the standing army with the armed people, which implies universal service.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: The Manifesto states that workingmen have no country and that national differences are vanishing under capitalism.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed by Marx; inferred from the Manifesto's concern for the proletariat, who are the usual targets of such state violence.

close-ties-china.rationale: Anachronistic: Marx wrote nothing on a choice between China and the United States, and the Manifesto's internationalism points both ways.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The Manifesto holds that the proletariat has no country and aims to end national antagonisms, so kin-nation protection is rejected.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: The Manifesto calls for abolition of property in land and the use of rents for public purposes, which fits common ownership of natural resources.

self-ownership.rationale: Inferred from Marx's critique that wage labour is a forced sale of labour power; the Gotha Programme also notes labour is not the only source of wealth.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's call for a heavy progressive income tax in preference to taxes that fall on workers' consumption.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's call for free education for all children and common provision rather than charity for the poor.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from the Commune, where delegates were recallable and direct, though Marx also urged the proletariat to organise its own party.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's view that the state serves the bourgeoisie as a whole, though adherents would hold that abolishing capital is the real remedy.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: The Gotha Programme critique wants religion made a private matter and puts class rather than creed at the centre of politics.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: The Manifesto says all that is solid melts into air and that old prejudices are swept away, so tradition is not something to return to.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's attack on the bourgeois family and women as instruments of production.

national-resource-control.rationale: Inferred from the Manifesto's centralisation of the means of production in the hands of the workers' state.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Marx rejects judging distribution by formal entitlement; the Gotha Critique treats equal bourgeois right as a defect and holds distribution follows the mode of production, ending in distribution by need.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the Manifesto backs a heavy progressive tax, but adherents would also call a levy on finance a reform that leaves capital's rule intact, so they split.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the view that class exploitation is the basic structure of oppression, with racial divisions fostering bourgeois rule, so racism is not downplayed.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The Manifesto calls bourgeois jurisprudence the will of the ruling class; Marx rejected natural-law appeals to abstract justice, and his stance on legality was revolutionary rather than procedural.

automate-paid-work.rationale: The Gotha Critique looks to abundant productive forces and labour ceasing to be a mere means of life, and the Manifesto looks to growth in productive forces, which implies far less toil.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred: the Manifesto stresses the world market and proletarian unity across nations, not a balance among independent power centres.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Marx's analysis of value and exploitation rests on labour as the source of value; SEP presents this as central to his critique of capitalism.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The Manifesto says working men have no country and that national differences are vanishing, so patriotism is a bourgeois sentiment for Marx and Engels, though proletarians must first win political supremacy within a nation.

material-over-identity.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the primacy of class and material conditions in historical materialism, though Marx did not treat cultural issues as irrelevant.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Marx expected commodity production and exchange of products to end under common ownership; the Gotha Critique says producers do not exchange their products in the cooperative society.

missingStatements.text: Religion is an illusion that consoles people for real suffering and will fade once their material conditions are emancipated.
missingStatements.rationale: Marx called religion the opium of the people and wanted conscience liberated from it; SEP describes it as a response to material alienation that will fade.

missingStatements.text: Work under capitalism alienates people from what they produce, from their own activity and from one another.
missingStatements.rationale: Alienation of the worker from product, activity, others and species nature is central to Marx's critique of wage labour.

missingStatements.text: Capitalism has been a historically progressive force that created the material basis for a better society.
missingStatements.rationale: The Manifesto credits the bourgeoisie with creating vast productive forces and the proletariat that will succeed it.

notes: Positions on later issues (imperialism, vanguard party, one-country socialism, class struggle under socialism, party control of media and army) belong to Leninist and later strands and are answered at low confidence or neutral. Many modern-issue statements are anachronistic.
